description: Approves $1.77 million for Dutch Elm Disease management and equipment.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer questioned why funding was a post-budget ask.
Saskatoon's urban canopy and neighborhood aesthetics are at significant risk.
City transitions to active, long-term Dutch Elm Disease management model.
Long-term financial plan for Dutch Elm Disease management remains unclear.
SOS Trees supported the budget request and outlined strategy.
Loss of urban canopy will have devastating environmental and visual impact.
Administration will provide seasonal updates on Dutch Elm Disease management.

description: City acquires 130 Idylwyld North for a drop-in center.
Federal funds cover $1.635M purchase; $350K for renovations.
New drop-in center opens November 2026, replacing 325 Avenue C South.

chips.text: Approved (7-4)
7 for, 4 against
A new 90-space childcare center is opening across the street from the proposed site.
Administration's recommendation to proceed was unchanged by identifying a nearby 90-child daycare.
Federal funding requires the property to be used for homelessness response for five years.
A detailed budget for the $350,000 renovations was not available at the time of the vote.
Multiple businesses and residents spoke against the location
Councillor Davies stated the Idylwyld location is not a better solution than the Avenue C site.
A speaker flagged potential liability risks due to the daycare's proximity to the drop-in center.
The building's two units could allow for separate spaces for men and women.
Administration committed to developing a coordinated safety plan with neighbors and businesses.
